messages:
security-bot: 🚨 Alert: spike in POST /v1/token across multiple regions detected. Unusual IP churn and high success rate. surge: ~1.2k req/s, success ~55%. WAF anomalies flagged. Auto-page to sec-oncall.

maria (sec-oncall): I'm on it. seeing identical user-agent fingerprints + rapid rotate of x-forwarded-for. Looks like credential stuffing hitting token refresh + primary auth.

lee (sre): Confirmed. Downstream auth-db RPS up, queue length on auth-service up 6x, some timeouts. Dedicated GPU pools unaffected. Impact is auth latencies (~600ms -> 2s) for affected customers.

jonas (infra): Collecting top offending IPs and ASNs. Many from small cloud providers/proxy networks. Will push to WAF block list first, then rate-limit per-IP.

maria (sec-oncall): Proposed mitigations (live):
1) WAF: block obvious proxy ASNs and known bad UA pattern.
2) Per-IP rate limit: 10 req/min for /v1/token for new/anonymous accounts.
3) Global burst throttle: reduce token endpoint burst to protect auth-service.
4) Temporarily disable password-based token refresh for non-verified apps (keep refresh via OAuth client).
5) Open a dedicated ticket for customer-impact and comms.

ranjit (product): Need to avoid breaking legitimate refreshes for active customers. Can we scope the disable to unverified clients + new accounts?

lee (sre): Yes. We can scope by client_id + recent-last-login. Suggest quick rules: if client_verified=false AND account_age<7d then block password flows.

jonas (infra): Pushing initial WAF rule now. Rule content (Cloud WAF):

```
# block high-entropy UA + small-cloud ASN
if (request.headers['User-Agent'] =~ /python-requests|curl|massclient/) {
  block()
}
if (ip.asn in [36561, 45595, 39832]) {
  block()
}
```

jonas (infra): Applied. Starting to see drop in offending RPS from blocked IPs.

lee (sre): Applying per-IP rate limit on token endpoint (quick CLI):

```
redwoodctl rate-limit set --route "/v1/token" --scope ip --limit 10/min --burst 20 --reason "mitigate credential stuffing"
```

lee (sre): Done. Also added sticky prefix-based KV cache to reduce repeated DB hits for identical tokens.

maria (sec-oncall): Good. Next: quota adjustments for high-volume API keys that look like abusers — throttle to 1 req/s with override review. jonas, can you apply temporary quota cap per api_key?

jonas (infra): Applied per-key caps for keys with >1000 token calls in last 5m. CLI: `redwoodctl quota update --filter "token_calls>1000" --cap 1/s`

ranjit (product): Can we whitelist a handful of high-value customers so we don't introduce friction? I can DM the list.

maria (sec-oncall): Yes, whitelist by api_key list. Send me the five IDs. Also starting customer-impact review.

ops-bot: Deploy job 12984 started: auth-service horizontal scale + patch rate-limiter config.

lee (sre): Scaling auth-service x2 to cope with residual load. Patch rolled with zero-downtime.

jonas (infra): Adding a temporary CAPTCHA challenge for interactive web login flows from suspect IPs. Implementation: Cloud WAF challenge mode + header X-Require-CAPTCHA.

maria (sec-oncall): Early metrics: overall token request volume down 70% after WAF + rate limits. Auth error rate stabilized. Some legitimate customers reported slower refreshes — mostly new signups and mobile clients.

ranjit (product): Customer-impact summary draft: ~0.6% of active customers experienced degraded token refresh over 25 mins. No data exfil observed, primarily failed login attempts. Will prepare comms if we need to notify.

lee (sre): Mitigation rollback plan: revert strict per-ip rate-limit and ASNs after 2h if no resurgence. Keep per-key caps until manual review.

maria (sec-oncall): Action items: 
- jonas: keep WAF blocks + CAPTCHA for 2h, collect top 200 IPs & ASNs (due +20m).
- lee: monitor auth DB queue and SLOs, be ready to scale down.
- ranjit: compile whitelist of trusted api_keys (due +10m).
- me: create incident ticket and customer-impact doc, escalate to security ops if credential harvest evidence found.

maria (sec-oncall): Also creating a short-lived protective rule: block token refresh from IPs with >15 different accounts in last 10m. Will be more targeted than global block.

jonas (infra): Implemented that rule at edge. Example snippet we used in edge-config: `if ip.address has >15 account_ids in 10m then challenge`

ops-bot: Note: deploy 12984 succeeded and new rate-limit config active in all regions.

lee (sre): We should log the event for model-fine-tuning: attack patterns look automated; add to evals corpus.

maria (sec-oncall): Agreed. Saving request samples to secure bucket: s3://redwood-incidents/1968275300/requests.gz (access: sec-oncall + infra + legal).

ranjit (product): Any immediate customer comms? I recommend 'we briefly rate-limited high-volume suspicious activity, some customers may need to re-auth'. Draft in #marketing-ops?

maria (sec-oncall): I'll sync with support for canned response. No broad outage, just localized friction.

lee (sre): Handing off to night oncall in 30m. If anything flares, esk to sec-oncall pager.

maria (sec-oncall): Handing to @lee for post-mitigation monitoring. Leaving notes in the incident ticket. Good job team :thumbsup:

lee (sre): Taking over. Summary saved to ticket INC-1968275300. Continuing monitoring.

security-bot: Incident thread closed for active mitigation. Monitoring still active.
